questions.text_english:
(1) Gossip. All humans partake in some form, despite the age-old adage, If you have nothing nice to say, don't say anything at all.Whether it's workplace chatter, the sharing of family news or group texts between friends, it's inevitable that anyone who participates in the above, talks about other people.

(2) People tend to think of gossip as synonymous with malicious rumours, put-downs, or the breathless propagation of a tabloid scoop. But researchers often define it more broadly as talking about people who aren't present,says an assistant professor of psychology. It's something that comes very naturally to usan integral part of conversation, information sharing, and even community building.

(3) It's not necessarily negative, adds a professor of psychology. It can be positive or neutral.some researchers argue that gossip helped our ancestors survive. Evolutionary psychologists first pioneered this idea, comparing gossip to the grooming primates engage in as a means of bonding.

(4) People are usually resistant to thinking about gossip as anything but bad. It is true that there are some types of gossip that should be avoided, such as gossip that is purely harmful and serves no purpose like mean comments on someone's way of dressing. In such a scenario no one benefits. Gossip can also be both active and passive. Active gossiping refers to directly sharing negative information about someone else. An active gossiper initiates the conversation and actively spreads it. Passive gossiping on the other hand involves more subtle behaviour like hinting, dropping suggestive comments or participating in gossip by listening without actively contributing, but still allowing the gossip to spread through their presence.

(5) It's interesting to note that gossiping also says something about relationships people have with one another. The act of gossiping often implies a level of trust and closeness with someone, which are key aspects of a good friendship.

(6) Research has found that gossip can stave off loneliness, while other studies have found it can facilitate bonding and closeness and serve as a form of entertainment. So, keep on talking. And when your conversation turns to gossip, as it inevitably will, remember that some good can come of it - with the right intentions, of course.

sub_questions.text_english: By the phrase 'put-downs' the writer means _______ in paragraph (2).
sub_questions.solution: The writer uses the phrase 'put-downs' to refer to malicious or derogatory comments intended to belittle others and lower their social standing.

sub_questions.text_english: Despite the bad reputation of 'gossip', mention any two benefits that it offers.
sub_questions.solution: Two key benefits of gossip are that it facilitates social bonding and closeness between individuals, and it serves as a form of social entertainment that can help alleviate loneliness.

sub_questions.text_english: The concern the phrase 'It's something that comes very naturally to us' points towards is about A. that some types of gossip should be avoided. B. that gossip can be viewed as part of our daily interaction and bonding.

options.A: that some types of gossip should be avoided.
options.B: that gossip can be viewed as part of our daily interaction and bonding.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct because the phrase emphasizes that gossip is an innate, natural part of human communication, integral to daily interaction and community building, rather than merely a malicious act.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the analogy with one word from paragraph (2). Praise: Commend :: _______ : Malevolent (A) Scoop (B) Propagation (C) Malicious (D) Conversation
sub_questions.solution: The analogy is based on synonyms. 'Malicious' is the direct synonym for 'Malevolent' explicitly used in paragraph 2.

sub_questions.text_english: What type of gossip does the author disapprove of and why?
sub_questions.solution: The author disapproves of gossip that is purely harmful, such as making mean comments about someone's appearance. This is because such gossip serves no productive purpose, is malicious, and ultimately benefits no one.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following suitably with one difference between the author's opinion and that of people about gossip. Generally, people do not readily accept _______.
sub_questions.solution: Generally, people do not readily accept gossip as anything but bad, whereas the author argues it can often be neutral or even positive in the right context.

sub_questions.text_english: Sentence 1: Ranjan told Raman and Shah the sensational facts he had heard about his friend Vineet from others. Sentence 2: Kumar stayed silent while his friends criticized his close friend Vijay in his absence. Classify as active or passive participation.
sub_questions.solution: Sentence 1 is active participation because Ranjan initiates and spreads the negative information. Sentence 2 is passive participation because Kumar listens without contributing but allows the gossip to continue through his silence.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the author say that gossip is a reflection of relationships?
sub_questions.solution: The author says this because the act of sharing gossip often implies a level of trust, intimacy, and closeness between the individuals involved, which are essential components of friendship.

sub_questions.text_english: Choose the correct option: gossip can 'stave off loneliness'. The above statement is true as: (A) we always enjoy talking ill of others. (B) we believe what we read about people in the print media. (C) we are free to talk loosely in the absence of the person. (D) in order to gossip, you need to feel close to people.

options.A: we always enjoy talking ill of others.
options.B: we believe what we read about people in the print media.
options.C: we are free to talk loosely in the absence of the person.
options.D: in order to gossip, you need to feel close to people.

sub_questions.solution: Option D is correct because gossiping facilitates connection and fosters the closeness required to share information, thus reducing individual feelings of loneliness.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following suitably: The author puts forth the fact that man can never _______ gossiping.
sub_questions.solution: The sentence is completed as: The author puts forth the fact that man can never stop gossiping, as it is an inevitable and natural part of human social life.

questions.text_english:
(1) Introduction: Humans are social creatures with a deep desire to interact with one another. Recent developments in technology have made it possible for billions of people worldwide to use cell phones to satisfy this need. The current study aims to analyse the impact of smartphone use among various categories of people in Kerala, India. The present study will provide an insight into the extent and magnitude of people's reliance on smartphones to communicate in this modern age and the dwindling nature of social relationships.

(2) Methodology: A google form created questionnaire was used to gather information on the subject from a sample of participants who were from various districts in Kerala, India.

(3) Survey Examination: Among the 131 study participants, 66 were men and the remaining 65 were women. For convenience, the study considered only the main purpose for which a smartphone is used by any given individual.

(4) Results: 
S.No | Purpose | Frequency | Percentage
1. | Academic | 21 | 11-11
2. | Communication | 56 | 29-63
3. | Entertainment | 48 | 25-40
4. | Others | 64 | 33-86
Individuals differed in their interests and preferences regarding their choice of communication medium. Some preferred direct conversation, while others conveyed their messages through virtual mediums of communication, that did not involve any face-to-face interaction.

(5) Implications for Interventions: It was observed that individuals were interested in using their smartphones even when they were dining. This constant use can have several disadvantages such as reckless use of mobile phones, including prolonged hours of radiation exposure, over-calorie intake due to binge eating, leading to obesity, and other health problems. It is also a vital tool to achieve social progress. The use of phones while travelling can sometimes detract from an individual's enjoyment of the serenity of the environment, the scenic beauty of picnic spots, and affect the way an individual behaves and interacts with his or her co-travellers.

(6) Conclusion: It is true that most of the population under different age and gender categories use smartphones every day, but there is no significant fall in the duration spent in direct face-to-face conversation with fellow beings, except in very few individuals. The majority of people agree that traditional face-to-face communication is more comfortable, reliable, and expressive than text messages, phone calls, or electronic mail.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following suitably. In the introduction, the researcher links the digital age with the impact of social media on mental health to highlight _______.

fill_values: the dwindling nature of social relationships

sub_questions.solution: The researcher highlights the potential for modern technology to impact the quality and depth of human connections, often leading to a decrease in meaningful social relationships.

sub_questions.text_english: What would the following be classified as? 'To examine waste management practices across various age groups in detail.' Select the appropriate response: (A) Primary purpose (B) Secondary objective (C) Method of analysis (D) Research outcome
sub_questions.solution: This statement defines the core reason and the main objective or primary purpose of the case study.

sub_questions.text_english: Give two points to support how the case study explored various age groups.
sub_questions.solution: The case study explored age groups by using a survey that included participants from different demographics—ranging from teenagers to elderly citizens. Additionally, it systematically analyzed these groups to identify specific waste management trends, habits, and preferences unique to each stage of life.

sub_questions.text_english: Paragraph 5 uses words like 'motivations' and 'interventions'. Classify the following sentences as 'motivation' or 'intervention': (A) Targeting educational campaigns towards teenagers and young adults could empower them to adopt sustainable waste management practices. (B) Efforts to enhance the infrastructure for segregation at source.
sub_questions.solution: (A) is an intervention, and (B) is also an intervention. Interventions are specific proactive measures or programs implemented to change behavior or improve systems.

sub_questions.text_english: Radhika actively participates in school programmes that promote recycling. Her neighbour, Ragini, prefers recycling and reusing items for their environmental benefits. However, their neighbour Mrs. Gupta sticks to traditional disposal methods out of habit. Select the option that identifies the correct demographic they belong to: (A) Radhika - middle-aged; Ragini - young adult; Mrs. Gupta - elderly (B) Radhika - teenager; Ragini - young adult; Mrs. Gupta - elderly (C) Radhika - young adult; Ragini - elderly; Mrs. Gupta - middle-aged (D) Radhika - elderly; Ragini - middle-aged; Mrs. Gupta - teenager

options.A: Radhika - middle-aged; Ragini - young adult; Mrs. Gupta - elderly
options.B: Radhika - teenager; Ragini - young adult; Mrs. Gupta - elderly
options.C: Radhika - young adult; Ragini - elderly; Mrs. Gupta - middle-aged
options.D: Radhika - elderly; Ragini - middle-aged; Mrs. Gupta - teenager

sub_questions.solution: Radhika matches the teenager group (school participation), Ragini matches young adults (recycling/reuse/sustainability), and Mrs. Gupta matches the elderly demographic (traditional habits).

sub_questions.text_english: Why is the percentage to adopt recycling methods higher among young adults?
sub_questions.solution: The percentage is higher among young adults because they are strongly motivated by sustainability, personal convenience, and a sense of social responsibility.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyze how targeted interventions based on the diverse waste management preferences of different age groups can lead to improved environmental outcomes.
sub_questions.solution: Targeted interventions address specific demographic barriers—such as educational campaigns for teenagers to overcome lack of awareness, and improved infrastructure for those who prioritize convenience. By aligning programs with specific motivations, stakeholders can ensure higher participation rates, leading to more effective waste management and improved environmental outcomes.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the ultimate goal for stakeholders, based on the insight from the study? (A) Increase profitability through enhanced recycling infrastructure (B) Build cleaner urban environments (C) Reduce the cost of waste management (D) Expand the range of recycling programmes available

options.A: Increase profitability through enhanced recycling infrastructure
options.C: Reduce the cost of waste management
options.D: Expand the range of recycling programmes available

sub_questions.solution: As stated in the conclusion, the collaborative goal of all stakeholders is to build cleaner and more sustainable urban environments for future generations.

questions.text_english: (a) Waste management in your colony is becoming an issue of grave concern. Write a letter to the editor of a local daily, discussing the reasons for poor waste management. Also suggest ways to resolve the problem. You are Shireen/Sahil of Prestige Colony, Rahagarh. OR (b) You are Arati/Ashok from New Colony, Bamapur. You read the advertisement regarding the position of an Event Manager at Raleigh Planners and wish to apply. Write your application along with your bio-data.
questions.solution:
Prestige Colony
Rahagarh
June 6, 2026

The Editor
The Daily News
Rahagarh

Subject: Grave concern regarding poor waste management in Prestige Colony

Sir,

I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the deteriorating waste management situation in Prestige Colony. Despite being a residential area, the lack of awareness about waste segregation and an inefficient collection system has led to overflowing bins, attracting pests and creating severe environmental pollution. It is unacceptable that such conditions persist in a modern city. To resolve this, I urge the local municipal authorities to upgrade our waste collection infrastructure immediately. Furthermore, community-led initiatives are vital. We must conduct awareness drives to teach residents about the importance of segregating dry and wet waste. Civic responsibility starts at home, and the local administration must actively support these efforts by providing the necessary resources. I hope that through this letter, the concerned authorities take prompt action to restore cleanliness and health to our colony.

Yours faithfully,
Shireen

questions.text_english: (a) In today's fast-paced world, fitness apps have become a popular tool for tracking and improving health. Write an article for your school magazine educating the youth on the pros and cons of fitness apps. You are Kirti/Kirat, a school fitness coach. OR (b) Write a comprehensive report detailing the activities undertaken by students as part of the International Women's Day celebrations. You are Aarushi/Aarav, a student of class XII and a member of the school magazine editorial board.
questions.solution:
PROS AND CONS OF FITNESS APPS
By Kirti, School Fitness Coach

In our digital age, fitness apps have transformed into essential tools for tracking physical health. They are increasingly popular among youth because they provide personalized workout routines, track calories, and monitor heart rates in real time. However, blindly following these apps can have significant drawbacks. Many users lack professional supervision, which can lead to improper technique and injury. Additionally, these apps often raise major privacy concerns as they collect sensitive personal health data, leaving users vulnerable to data theft. While apps can motivate us to stay active, they should be used with caution, acting as a supplement rather than a substitute for professional guidance. True fitness requires a balance between technology, common sense, and listening to our bodies. By using these tools judiciously, we can work toward a healthier lifestyle without compromising our well-being or digital privacy.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) The expression 'we will all keep still' reflects : (A) the poet's willingness to keep quiet. (B) the significance of stillness. (C) the poet's appeal for collective engagement. (D) the purpose of counting up to twelve.

options.A: the poet's willingness to keep quiet.
options.C: the poet's appeal for collective engagement.
options.D: the purpose of counting up to twelve.

sub_questions.solution: The poet uses 'we will all' to appeal for collective, global engagement in a moment of shared peace and introspection.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) What does the poet want us to stop?
sub_questions.solution: The poet wants us to stop speaking in any language and to stop moving our arms, meaning he wants us to cease all aggressive and hurried activities.

(B) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true, but the reason is false. (D) The assertion is false, but the reason is true.

options.B: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
options.C: The assertion is true, but the reason is false.

sub_questions.solution: The poet urges us to count to twelve so that we can have a synchronized moment to stop all activity and achieve stillness.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) 'Counting to twelve' is suggested as a _______ (synchronized/disorganized) effort for everybody to keep quiet.
sub_questions.solution: Counting is a 'synchronized' effort because it ensures that everyone pauses simultaneously, creating a collective experience of peace.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) How can the message in the excerpt, about silence and stillness be applied to promote peace in today's world?
sub_questions.solution: The message applies by encouraging people to pause their frenzied, aggressive routines, allowing for the reflection needed to resolve conflicts and foster empathy.

questions.text_english: Answer any five of the following six questions in 40-50 words each:
questions.solution:
Robert Frost highlights the selfishness of city dwellers by showing their total indifference to the roadside stand owners. While the rich travel in their luxury cars, they are too preoccupied with their own comfort to notice or care about the rural inhabitants' struggle for survival, highlighting a stark urban-rural divide. 

Sophie's father is a pragmatist who views her dreams of opening a boutique as delusional. He responds with dismissive cynicism, viewing her aspirations as unrealistic fantasies that hold no value in their working-class life, reinforcing the gap between her inner imagination and his harsh reality.

Kothamangalam Subbu was considered the 'No. 2' at Gemini Studios because of his immense versatility and loyalty. He was an efficient troubleshooter, a creative poet, and a skilled actor who could provide multiple solutions for any scene, making him indispensable to the Boss.

Rajkumar Shukla was resolute because he did not give up until he achieved his purpose. Despite Gandhi’s busy schedule, he doggedly followed him from place to place—to Cawnpore, Ahmedabad, and then to the ashram—until Gandhi finally agreed to accompany him to Champaran.

Umberto Eco displays modesty by acknowledging that his work is a result of trial and error. He does not claim intellectual superiority, but instead shares the process of his research, including his failures, showing his human side rather than presenting himself as a flawless academic genius.

Beauty is 'everlasting' because it serves as an eternal source of joy. Keats notes that as life gets filled with gloom and despondency, a beautiful object acts as a healing force. It creates a lasting impression on our dark spirits, offering inspiration and comfort forever.

questions.text_english: Answer any two of the following three questions in 40-50 words each:
questions.solution:
Tishani Doshi feels she is walking into a 'giant ping-pong ball' because Antarctica is completely devoid of human markers like trees, billboards, or buildings. The landscape is a stark, vast expanse of white, making one feel tiny and disconnected from the familiar world.

Charley realizes Sam can't return to his old business because Sam has completely embraced his desire to escape reality. By settling in Galesburg, 1894, Sam has effectively abandoned his practice, choosing the fantasy of a simpler past over the modern world he once professionally analyzed.

Derry enters Mr. Lamb’s garden seeking solitude, believing it to be empty. His intent is not to disturb anyone, but to escape from society’s judgment regarding his burnt face. He enters the garden simply because he feels it is a place where he can hide from others' pity.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words: (a) How do the characters of Rajkumar Shukla from 'Indigo' and William Douglas from 'Deep Water' compare and contrast in terms of their courage, constraints, and determination? OR (b) Analyse the lesson 'Lost Spring' and the poem 'A Roadside Stand' with reference to social inequality and the indifferent attitude of society.
questions.solution:
Rajkumar Shukla and William Douglas are both powerful examples of determination, though their journeys differ significantly. Shukla’s courage was rooted in his unyielding commitment to justice for sharecroppers. Despite his lack of education and resources, his determination to bring Gandhi to Champaran forced the hands of colonial authorities, proving that individual persistence can overcome massive political barriers. 

William Douglas, conversely, faced an internal, psychological constraint—an intense, paralyzing fear of water. His journey was one of self-conquest. Through disciplined, grueling training, he pushed past his terror to reclaim his life and freedom. While Shukla fought for a community's rights against an external oppressor, Douglas fought his own internal demons. Both men illustrate that whether the struggle is communal or personal, relentless will and courage can surmount any obstacle, shifting one’s destiny through sheer, unwavering resolve.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words: (a) In what way did Mr. Lamb's ideas of watching, listening, and thinking help Derry change his perspective towards life? OR (b) According to Tishani Doshi in 'Journey to the end of the Earth', man's supremacy over nature is responsible for the problems we face today. Support your answer with evidence from the text.
questions.solution:
Mr. Lamb's philosophy of watching, listening, and thinking plays a pivotal role in transforming Derry’s life. Derry enters the garden filled with self-pity and bitterness due to his facial disfigurement. Mr. Lamb, despite his own disability, remains vibrant and optimistic, teaching Derry that life is about more than just a physical appearance. By encouraging Derry to watch the world around him, listen to the sounds of nature, and think deeply about his perceptions, Lamb challenges Derry’s defensive mindset.

He shows Derry that beauty is subjective and that his disability need not define his identity. Derry learns that he can choose how he interacts with the world. Through Lamb’s gentle guidance and philosophical wisdom, Derry realizes that he is not a prisoner of his circumstances. He begins to see the potential for joy and connection, eventually finding the courage to return to the garden, signaling a fundamental shift from self-loathing to self-acceptance and a newfound appreciation for the richness of existence.
